options.text: Any rock that contains a metal
A rock containing enough metal compound to make extraction economically worthwhile
A pure metal found in the ground
A metal oxide that has been processed in a factory

questions.explanation: An ore is a rock that contains enough of a metal compound to make it economically worthwhile to extract the metal. Not all rocks containing metals are ores -- the concentration must be high enough to justify the cost of extraction.

questions.stem: Why can iron be extracted by reduction with carbon but sodium cannot?

options.text: Iron is more reactive than carbon, so carbon can take its oxygen
Sodium is below carbon in the reactivity series
Iron is below carbon in the reactivity series, so carbon can reduce its oxide; sodium is above carbon, so it cannot
Sodium does not form an oxide compound

questions.explanation: Iron is below carbon in the reactivity series, meaning carbon is more reactive than iron and can remove oxygen from iron oxide. Sodium is above carbon in the reactivity series, meaning sodium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot remove oxygen from sodium oxide. Electrolysis must be used for sodium instead.
